protocol.question: Does external sensory current produce neural activity outside the directly stimulated neurons, and is that activity attributable to the visual schedule rather than player defaults?

C0.description: no external current; same graph, duration, timestep, seed and initial state. input_schedule is None.

C1.description: 100 neutral TemporalFrames at 30 fps with GameState.neutral(); only the four player-default features are active. No object detections and no object-derived features.

C2.description: the same cached visual frames as C3 with every player-default feature disabled; hold and visual event pulses restricted to the ten non-player features. Not pulses-only.

C3.description: full sensory replay of the cached visual frames with all fourteen features active; must reproduce the archived Phase 3B.2C scheduler signature and spike-count hash.

comparison.note: These are whole-condition contrasts of a deterministic recurrent network. They are descriptive; subtracting conditions does not identify additive contributions.

limitations: Spikes are model output under configured assumptions, not measured biological activity. The connectome is fixed and no plasticity is used.
The mapped neurons are experimental input populations drawn from predicted FlyWire annotations, not an identified sensory pathway.
Distance and lane are image geometry, not game measurements.
C0 with zero background, zero noise and a resting initial potential is the no-input floor; any activity in C1-C3 is driven by injected current and its synaptic consequences.

One deterministic run per condition is executed per repeat. There is no sampling distribution across seeds, so the preregistered analysis is descriptive; no p-value is computed and no significance is claimed.
Subtracting conditions does not identify a linear contribution: the network is recurrent and nonlinear, so C3-C0 is a whole-schedule contrast, not a sum of C1-C0 and C2-C1.
No action is selected anywhere in this experiment.
action_selection: none; the chain ends at sensory current injection
